_comment: CLOCK-INVARIANCE CONTROL for the freshness evaluation. Identical to
freshness_canon_300ms.json except that every TIME quantity is scaled by
k = 40 = 1000 MHz / 25 MHz, and the profiles are read from gen25/,
exported from the SAME measured cycles at the real 25-30 MHz Alveo
bitstream frequency instead of an assumed 1 GHz.
Purpose: the headline result is stated in milliseconds derived as
cycles/1e6, i.e. at a clock the hardware does not run at. If durations and
periods both scale by k the schedule is a pure time-rescaling, so every
RATE (output_valid_rate, deadline_success_rate) must be identical and the
conclusion does not depend on the clock -- it depends on the ratio of
compute time to period. This config tests that claim instead of asserting
it. A mismatch would mean the solver is not scale-invariant (absolute
tolerances, float error) and the 1 GHz framing would be load-bearing.
At 25 MHz the same workload is a slower robot: 400 ms control period,
2 s perception period, 12 s epoch. That is the honest restatement -- the
phenomenon is real at the true frequency, just at 1/40 the rate.

epoch._comment: Read by the freshness sweep, not by the scheduler.

_comment: p_core_speedup is 1.0 because both clusters have real measured profiles;
nothing is derived from the other by a ratio.
Hard-critical consumer. 0.546 ms of work in a 10 ms window, and the same
cost on both backends (kernels/gemmini has no linear kernel, so an
all-linear model falls back to the same scalar reference either side).
It therefore has no placement preference, which is why 'isolate control
on a separate core' is not one of the protection mechanisms.
Producer in the hard-validity chain. 17.973 ms on gemmini vs 241.462 ms
on rvv_opu -- a 13.4x preference, so protecting it means reserving
gemmini for it, and that is exactly what contends with YOLO.
Soft interfering work. period = epoch/B spreads B releases across the
epoch; window_duration = epoch keeps the window loose so YOLO is
interference to be shed rather than a hard constraint that makes the
instance infeasible. 67.202 ms on gemmini vs 1069.004 ms on rvv_opu
(15.9x), so it wants the same backend DroNet needs. Soft utility is
counted as completed instances.

_edges_comment: MUST stay empty for the DroNet->MLP relationship. An entry here becomes a
MILP precedence constraint (workload_factory.py:733-760), which would force
the controller to wait for perception. A controller that blocks can never
consume a stale input -- it can only miss its deadline -- so a precedence
edge here would delete the phenomenon being measured. The freshness
relationship lives under freshness_edges and is evaluated post-hoc.

_comment: freshness_window here is the primary operating point only; the sweep
overrides it as phi = A0 + delta, where A0 is the MEASURED uncontended
input-age ceiling (60.546 ms for this grid) rather than the DroNet
period. Anchoring on the period instead would put phi below A0, and
the resulting staleness would come from the 50 ms sampling rate rather
than from contention. 70.5 = A0 + 10.
